articles.title: India's first orbital data center to be launched in 2028 - NewsBytes
articles.content: The mission will be carried out on SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket India's first orbital data center to be launched in 2028 By Dwaipayan Roy Sep 28, 2026 07:50 pm What's the story Hyderabad -based TakeMe2Space is gearing up to launch India's first orbital data center. The mission will be carried out on SpaceX 's Falcon 9 rocket in 2028. As part of the project, the company plans to deploy a constellation of six satellites over the next few years. The first two satellites will be launched as part of the Waymaker 2 rideshare mission, scheduled for late 2028. Mission details Waymaker 2 mission will see 2 satellites launched The Waymaker 2 mission will see two 100kg My Orbital Infrastructure (MOI) constellation satellites launched on a Falcon 9 rocket. The launch window is set for late 2028, following a launch service agreement with RIDE! space, the mission management company that booked the slot. "Everything we have flown so far has been about proving that compute belongs in orbit," said Ronak Kumar Samantray, founder and CEO of TakeMe2Space. Global alignment Project puts India on the map The upcoming mission also puts an Indian company on the map of a global movement to shift computing into orbit. The project will test if two spacecraft can function as one computer, a different approach from existing methods that usually involve a single spacecraft carrying a large processor. This is part of the company's larger plan to create an orbital data center in space. ADVERTISEMENT Past missions TakeMe2Space's 1st mission was launched in December 2024 TakeMe2Space's first mission, MOI-TD (Technology Demonstrator), was launched on December 30, 2024. It conducted over 20 experiments in low Earth orbit. The company has also scheduled two more launches for its data center-class satellites on October 1: MOI-1a and MOI-1b. Each satellite will generate about 1.5kW of power to run computing workloads in orbit, hosting 10 NVIDIA Thor GPUs and offering 100TB of storage capacity. ADVERTISEMENT Data sharing Satellites will be connected by optical inter-satellite links The two satellites will be connected by optical inter-satellite links, enabling them to share workloads and data. This is the first Indian mission designed to network computing across spacecraft rather than run it on a single satellite. Each satellite carries a multispectral imager with a ground sampling distance of about one meter, while the OrbitLab platform supplies onboard compute to process and analyze that imagery directly in orbit. articles.title: TakeMe2Space to launch satellites on SpaceX Falcon 9 for India's first orbital data centre test
articles.content: Aerospace & Defence 2 min read TakeMe2Space to launch satellites on SpaceX Falcon 9 for India’s first orbital data centre test Each 100-kg satellite will carry 10 Nvidia Thor GPUs and 100 TB storage; Waymaker 2 mission to test networked computing across spacecraft in late 2028 ETManufacturing Desk ETManufacturing Published On Sep 28, 2026 at 04:36 PM IST Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook A representative picture. Hyderabad-based space startup TakeMe2Space on Monday said it will launch two 100-kg satellites on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in late 2028 to test India's first networked orbital data centre. According to the Business Standard, the mission places an Indian company in a global race to move computing into orbit, where US-based Starcloud flew an Nvidia H100 graphics processing unit (GPU) in November 2025 and Google has said it will fly prototype Project Suncatcher satellites with Planet Labs by early 2027. Most of that work involves a single spacecraft, however, Waymaker 2 will test whether two can work as one computer. Advt It said that TakeMe2Space signed a launch service agreement with Paris-based RIDE! space, a launch mission management company that secured the slot for the firm. The satellites, part of its MOI (My Orbital Infrastructure) constellation, will fly on Waymaker 2, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rideshare mission to a sun-synchronous orbit at about 500 kilometres, with a launch window in late 2028. Ronak Kumar Samantray , founder and chief executive officer of TakeMe2Space, said that the company’s earlier missions were meant to show that computing belongs in orbit. “These two satellites are about proving it at a scale that pays,” he said. Each satellite will host 10 Nvidia Thor GPUs and 100 terabytes (TB) of storage, powered by about 1.5 kilowatt (kW) of generated electricity. The two will be linked by optical inter-satellite links to share workloads and data, the company said, making it the first Indian mission to network computing across spacecraft. Earth observation will be the first application. Each satellite carries a multispectral imager with a ground sampling distance of about 1 metre, and the company's OrbitLab platform will process the imagery in orbit, so users receive answers such as flood extent or a ship count rather than raw frames. Advt The satellites' power system uses silicon solar cells rather than gallium arsenide (GaAs), the industry standard for spacecraft. Silicon cells cost a fraction of GaAs cells, lowering the cost of each satellite and potentially the price customers pay to run workloads on the platform. articles.title: India's First Port-Based e-Methanol Production Facility at Kandla - Drishti IAS
articles.content: Assam Prev India’s First Port-Based e-Methanol Production Facility at Kandla 28 Sep 2026 3 min read Why in News? The foundation stone has been laid for India’s first port-based e-methanol production facility at Kandla, Gujarat , aimed at supplying green fuel to ships and supporting India’s transition towards cleaner maritime transport. The project involves an investment of around ₹2,300 crore and is expected to create about 3,500 employment opportunities . Key Points: Green Methanol Facility: A port-based e-methanol production facility will be developed at Kandla (Deendayal Port), Gujarat to produce cleaner marine fuel for ships. Investment & Employment: The project involves an investment of approximately ₹2,300 crore and is expected to generate around 3,500 jobs . E-Methanol: E-methanol, or electro-methanol , is produced using green hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide , with renewable electricity playing a key role in the production process. Green Shipping: The facility will support the use of low-carbon marine fuels , helping reduce greenhouse-gas emissions from the shipping sector. Kandla as Green Energy Hub: Deendayal Port Authority is being developed as a Green Hydrogen Hub under the National Green Hydrogen Mission . The port has also developed infrastructure for green-fuel handling and methanol bunkering. Methanol Bunkering: Kandla has already advanced its methanol bunkering capabilities and conducted a shore-to-ship methanol bunkering trial in April 2026. National Green Hydrogen Mission: The project complements India's efforts to develop green hydrogen derivatives such as green methanol and green ammonia for sectors that are difficult to electrify directly. Net Zero Target: The initiative supports India's commitment to achieve Net Zero carbon emissions by 2070 and promotes the decarbonisation of the maritime sector. Maritime Trade: Port-based production and supply of green fuel can facilitate green bunkering infrastructure , reduce fuel logistics requirements and support India's participation in emerging green shipping corridors. Green Methanol Standards: India notified Green Methanol Standards in February 2026, specifying that green methanol must meet prescribed greenhouse-gas emission thresholds. The standard sets a limit of 0.44 kg CO₂ equivalent per kg of methanol . Read More: National Green Hydrogen Mission, Net Zero Target Print PDF Print This Article Prev

articles.title: TakeMe2Space MOI-1A: India's First Orbital Computing Satellite Explained - Jagran Josh
articles.content: India is slated to enter a fresh phase of commercial space computing as Hyderabad-based startup TakeMe2Space prepares to launch MOI-1A, an orbital computing satellite, aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission on October 1. The company regards the spacecraft as India’s first orbital computing satellite, which is developed to process data in space instead of sending enormous volumes of raw information to Earth. What is orbital computing? Traditional Earth-observation satellites capture data and transmit it to ground stations, where computers process it. This requires bandwidth, especially when satellites generate large datasets. MOI-1A is manufactured to perform edge computing in orbit. It will carry Nvidia Orin NX processors and run artificial-intelligence models on the satellite. Instead of transmitting complete datasets, the spacecraft can analyse information in orbit and send results to users on Earth. How will MOI-1A work? The sub-50-kg satellite has around 150 watts of available power, according to founder and CEO Ronak Samantray. Customers will be able to upload containerised AI models to the spacecraft. As the satellite passes over a target area, these models can process Earth-observation data and transmit analysis rather than the entire dataset. This could lower the volume of information downloaded and possibly lower costs for customers that otherwise transfer and process enormous satellite imagery. Who will use the satellite? TakeMe2Space said it has secured 23 customers for the mission, including geographic information-system companies and educational institutions. Potential applications include agriculture, mining, supply-chain management and insurance. US-based space-data analytics company Little Place Labs is among the customers. The company also is aiming at orbital cold storage for critical information, with potential applications in financial services and defence. TakeMe2Space: From demonstration to commercial mission TakeMe2Space previously showcased its technology in orbit. The company says its 2024 mission validated uploading applications and performing AI inference in space before downloading results. A later MOI-1 satellite was lost after a launch-vehicle third-stage failure. The startup is eyeing bigger satellites from 2027 and aims to build a networked constellation. Its longer-term plan is to operate six satellites capable of processing Earth-observation data in orbit. Why does it matter for India’s private space sector? The mission comes as India’s private space sector expands following reforms opening more opportunities for non-government companies. The Department of Space said in August that around 440 space-tech startups were registered on the DPIIT Start-up India portal. MOI-1A embodies a shift from satellites mainly gathering and transmitting data toward spacecraft that can decode information before sending it down. If successful, the approach could facilitate faster satellite-derived intelligence while lowering the burden on ground infrastructure.

articles.title: “ India's First LNG Powered Train Is Here”: Amit Shah Flags Off New Railway Initiative
articles.content: Share Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Email Support Independent Journalism Support Goemkarponn’s mission for fearless journalism. Donate Now New Delhi: India has introduced its first LNG powered train, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel flagging off the train from Sabarmati in Ahmedabad on Sunday. The initiative marks a new step towards using alternative fuels in railway operations and reducing dependence on conventional diesel. The train operates on a dual fuel system that allows LNG to be used alongside diesel. Two 1,400 horsepower Driving Power Cars at the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot have been converted to run on the new system. More than 2,000 kilometres of field trials have been completed to assess the technology’s performance and reliability. The system can replace up to around 40 per cent of diesel consumption with LNG. Railway trial data indicates that the technology could lower fuel costs while also reducing emissions such as carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. Earlier assessments estimated annual savings of approximately Rs 11.9 lakh for a single Driving Power Car and around Rs 23.9 lakh for an eight coach rake. The converted power cars are equipped with LNG tanks holding about 2,200 litres, equivalent to approximately 850 to 900 kg of usable LNG. A full LNG tank is expected to support around 1,600 kilometres of operation, helping reduce the frequency of refuelling. The dual fuel system can switch between LNG and diesel depending on availability, while retaining the operational capabilities of conventional diesel engines. The LNG train was launched as part of a wider package of railway projects worth more than Rs 1,542 crore in Gujarat. The projects cover railway safety, signalling, freight infrastructure and additional line capacity. Shah also inaugurated a Rs 700 crore WAG 12 locomotive maintenance shed at Sabarmati and flagged off a WAG 12 electric locomotive. The programme included the commissioning of the indigenous Kavach train protection system on the Ahmedabad Palanpur and Ahmedabad Samakhiyali sections, automatic signalling on two sections and the launch of doubling work on the Sabarmati Sarkhej route. articles.title: India's First LNG-Powered Train Flagged off from Sabarmati - UdaipurTimes.com
articles.content: India’s First LNG-Powered Train Flagged off from Sabarmati Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurates projects worth Rs 1,472 crore and flags off country’s first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station By Razia Sanwari | Sep 28, 2026, 12:22 IST Join for live updates on WhatsApp UdaipurTimes, Sept 28, 2026 - Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah on Sunday, September 27, inaugurated development projects worth Rs 1,472 crore and flagged off the country’s first Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG)-powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. He also inaugurated the WAG-12 Maintenance Shed being constructed at a cost of Rs 700 crore for the maintenance of railway locomotive engines. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion. Addressing the programme, Union Home Minister Shah said the development works inaugurated will prove to be highly significant for the region in the coming days. The Kavach train protection system has been introduced on the Sabarmati–Kalol–Sabarmati rail section at a cost of Rs 48 crore to enhance safety. In addition, works have commenced for the implementation of Kavach on the Ahmedabad–Palanpur and Ahmedabad–Samakhiali rail sections, as well as the doubling of the Sabarmati–Sarkhej railway line. The LNG-powered train has been developed by the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Chennai and will operate from Sabarmati Junction to Mehsana. The use of LNG will also help lower fuel costs. LNG is cheaper than diesel, and according to Indian Railways' estimates, each DPC could help save approximately Rs 11.9 lakh per year. Accordingly, an eight-coach train could save around Rs 23.9 lakh annually. According to the Ahmedabad Railway Division, Indian Railways is using an LNG-based fuel system in a train’s Driving Power Car (DPC) for the first time. Under this technology, the engine can run on both LNG and diesel. Depending on fuel availability, the engine can use either of the two fuels. The new technology is expected to reduce diesel consumption by up to around 40% and also help reduce pollutants such as carbon dioxide (CO₂), nitrogen oxides (NOx) and particulate matter (PM). Two 1,400 HP DPCs have been converted to an LNG-diesel dual-fuel system. More than 2,000 km of field trials have already been conducted on both converted DPCs. Each DPC has been fitted with an LNG tank with a capacity of approximately 2,200 litres. The tank can hold around 950–1,000 kg of LNG. With this quantity of fuel, the train can travel approximately 440 km. articles.title: India's First LNG-Powered Train - INSIGHTS IAS
articles.content: Source: DD News Subject: Science and Technology Context: Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off India’s first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati, Gujarat, and inaugurated railway projects worth ₹1,472 crore, promoting dual-fuel traction, lower diesel consumption and reduced emissions. India's First LNG-Powered Train About India’s First LNG-Powered Train : What it is? An 8-coach passenger train (non-AC chair car) powered by a retrofitted LNG-diesel dual-fuel traction system , wherein cryogenic Liquefied Natural Gas substitutes up to 40% of conventional diesel consumption during line-haul operations. Location & Route: Flagged Off From: Sabarmati Railway Station, Ahmedabad Division (Western Railway), Gujarat. Inaugural Run : Operated between Sabarmati and Mahesana following conversion and testing at the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot. Aim: To decarbonise non-electrified and transitional rail routes, reduce expensive fossil-fuel diesel consumption, curb greenhouse gas and particulate emissions, and establish a cost-effective alternative fuel bridge toward Indian Railways’ goal of zero diesel consumption by 2030. Key Features: Dual-Fuel Traction: Two 1,400 HP Driving Power Cars (DPCs) have been retrofitted with electronically controlled gas-injection systems, enabling seamless switching between LNG and diesel without compromising engine performance. Cryogenic Fuel Storage: Each DPC carries a 2,200-litre insulated tank storing LNG at –162°C, providing sufficient fuel for approximately 444 km of daily operation. Emission Reduction: LNG-diesel traction reduces particulate matter (PM), nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions compared with conventional diesel-powered trains. Operational Cost Savings: Lower LNG prices offer estimated annual fuel savings of ₹11.9 lakh per DPC, amounting to approximately ₹23.9 lakh per eight-coach train. Extensive Safety Trials: Completed over 2,000 km of mainline trials under varying loads to assess cryogenic storage safety, pressure regulation and engine reliability before passenger operations. Significance: Complements railway electrification and hydrogen-train initiatives by offering a lower-emission alternative for non-electrified routes, shunting operations and freight transport. Reduces diesel consumption and potentially lowers crude-oil import dependence, while encouraging cleaner fuel adoption and diversification of India’s energy sources.

articles.content: Sectors News India’s First World Happiness Summit Concludes in Bengaluru, Promotes Pleasure, Peace and Purpose Positioned as India’s first World Happiness Summit, the day-long gathering was built around the idea that lasting happiness rests on three pillars, Pleasure, Peace and Purpose, the three Ps that give the brand its distinctive spelling. SMEStreet Edit Desk 28 Sep 2026 12:49 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 India’s first World Happiness Summit concluded today at New Horizon College of Engineering, Bengaluru, drawing a full-day audience into a conversation the country rarely pauses for: what does it truly take to be happy? Hosted by Happpy AiR – Atman in Ravi, the Happiness Ambassador, the summit brought together voices from entertainment, public life, entrepreneurship, spirituality, wellness and social leadership, and closed with a collective resolve to make Bengaluru the world’s happiest city. Positioned as India’s first World Happiness Summit, the day-long gathering was built around the idea that lasting happiness rests on three pillars, Pleasure, Peace and Purpose, the three Ps that give the brand its distinctive spelling. In a city celebrated as India’s technology and innovation capital, the summit sought to add a new dimension to Bengaluru’s identity, one that places wellbeing and fulfilment alongside ambition and growth. The morning session opened with the lighting of the lamp and an invocation, followed by Dr. Kiran Bedi on the Fundamentals of Happiness and Arjun Kapoor on The Secret of Happiness. A panel on Success and Happiness brought together Govind Mahtani, Shareen, Nikhil Kamath and Hema Sardesai, while a second panel explored the Manifestation of Happiness through Attraction with Dr. Amiett Kumar, Tarun Mishra, Rohit Khandelwal and Bhupendra Singh. Dr. Saamdu Chetri, a pioneer of Bhutan’s Gross National Happiness philosophy, offered a global perspective on measuring wellbeing over wealth. The afternoon carried the momentum forward with Sonu Sharma on How to Be Happy Every Day and Aisshwarya DKS on The Science of Happiness. A panel on The Art of Being Happy featured Sruthi Hariharan, Preetika Rao, Archika Sudhanshu, Dr. Aadhyaa Kumar and Renuka Goswami. Bringing the marquee sessions to a close, Shilpa Shetty spoke on The 3 Keys to Eternal Happiness, weaving together the wellness and positivity that have long defined her public life. Through the day, the summit also presented the Champion Awards, honouring individuals and organisations that foster positive work environments and champion the wellbeing of their people, extending the happiness conversation from the personal to the workplace. Reflecting on the day, Happpy AiR – Atman in Ravi, the Happiness Ambassador said, “Today, hundreds of people came together not to chase happiness, but to experience it, and that is the shift we set out to create. Happiness is not a reward we earn at the end of a long climb. It is a way of living, made of Pleasure, Peace and Purpose. articles.title: TakeMe2Space Plans India's First Orbital Data Centre Mission - GKToday
articles.content: Home TakeMe2Space Plans India’s First Orbital Data Centre Mission TakeMe2Space Plans India’s First Orbital Data Centre Mission September 28, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 Hyderabad-based TakeMe2Space plans to launch India’s first networked orbital data centre mission in 2028. The mission will use two 100-kilogram MOI (My Orbital Infrastructure) constellation satellites and a SpaceX Falcon 9 launch under the Waymaker 2 rideshare mission. Orbital Data Centre Concept An orbital data centre is a space-based computing system that processes data in orbit instead of sending all raw data to Earth. The planned mission will use optical inter-satellite links, which are laser-based communication links between satellites, to share workloads and data. Each satellite will carry 10 Nvidia Thor GPUs, 100 terabytes of storage, a one-metre multispectral imager, and power systems generating about 1.5 kilowatts. The satellites are designed to function as a distributed computer rather than as separate platforms. Mission Architecture and Launch Plan The launch service agreement has been signed with RIDE! space, a Paris-based launch mission management company. The company secured the Falcon 9 slot for a late-2028 launch window under the Waymaker 2 rideshare mission. The mission is planned as a networked constellation mission, which means the satellites will operate as a connected system in orbit. The use of a rideshare mission allows multiple payloads to share one launch vehicle. TakeMe2Space’s Earlier Missions TakeMe2Space launched its MOI-TD (Technology Demonstrator) mission on 30 December 2024. That mission carried out more than 20 experiments in low Earth orbit. The company’s MOI-1 satellite was lost in a PSLV-C62 launch failure in January 2026. The company has stated a longer-term plan to build a six-satellite constellation over the next few years. Important Facts for Exams Low Earth orbit generally refers to altitudes below 2,000 kilometres above Earth’s surface. Optical inter-satellite links use light-based communication between satellites and are different from radio-frequency links. Multispectral imagers capture data in multiple wavelength bands and are used in Earth observation. Rideshare missions carry more than one payload on the same launch vehicle. Key Technical Terms MOI stands for My Orbital Infrastructure. Nvidia Thor is a GPU platform used for high-performance computing applications. PSLV-C62 refers to an Indian Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle mission. articles.content: September 28, 2026 Shah flags off India’s first LNG-powered train in Gujarat Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pramod Kumar Singh Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah on Sunday launched railway development projects worth Rs 1,472 crore and flagged off India’s first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad. Shah said the new dual-fuel train will help protect the environment, make travel more convenient for passengers, and improve safety. The LNG-powered train is a Diesel Electric Multiple Unit with two 1,400 HP Driving Power Cars, converted at the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot to run on both diesel and LNG. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) is stored in cryogenic tanks of about 2,200 litres each and can replace almost 40 per cent of diesel use. The engines can switch between diesel and LNG as needed. Field trials have already covered over 2,000 km. Officials estimate yearly fuel savings of about Rs 11.9 lakh per power car and nearly Rs 23.9 lakh for an eight-coach train, along with lower emissions of carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulate matter. Shah said the launch is part of Indian Railways’ push to reduce diesel use. He pointed out that diesel consumption dropped from 293 crore litres in 2015-16 to 108 crore litres in 2024-25, with the goal of reaching zero by 2030. The network is now 99.6 per cent electrified, up from about 30 per cent before 2014. At the same event, Shah also opened a new WAG-12 locomotive maintenance shed in the Ahmedabad Division, built for Rs 700 crore. The new facility can service up to 300 high-power WAG-12 electric locomotives, each with 12,000 HP in a twin-section setup. These engines can haul as much freight as about 600 trucks, so one engine can now do the work that used to need two. The event also included the launch of a WAG-12 locomotive. Shah also laid the foundation stones for the Indian-made Kavach automatic train-protection system on 404 km of track: 157 km on the Ahmedabad-Palanpur section and 247 km on the Ahmedabad-Samakhiyali section, for Rs 411 crore. Kavach is already in use on the Sabarmati-Kalol section for Rs 48 crore to maintain safe distances between trains and increase route capacity. Shah also dedicated Automatic Block Signalling on the Sabarmati-Kalol-Bhandu Motidau and Sabarmati-Sanand-Jakhwada sections and laid the foundation stone for doubling the 21-km Sabarmati-Sarkhej line, a project costing Rs 313.27 crore and targeted for completion by March 2028. The doubling is expected to ease congestion and improve connectivity towards the Sarkhej-Dholera industrial corridor. At the ceremony, Shah remembered travelling through Sabarmati station in the past and said the area has changed completely. He praised Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and the local railway team for better passenger facilities, safety, and connections to Metro, bus services, and the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail station. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, and senior railway officials were also at the event. Shah said the projects are a joint effort for cleaner operations, more freight capacity,...

articles.title: India's First LNG-Powered Train Flagged Off - GKToday
articles.content: Home India’s First LNG-Powered Train Flagged Off India’s First LNG-Powered Train Flagged Off September 28, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 India’s first LNG-powered train was flagged off on 27 September 2026 from Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The train uses a diesel-plus-LNG dual-fuel system and runs with two 1,400 HP Driving Power Cars converted at the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot. LNG as a Railway Fuel LNG stands for liquefied natural gas, which is natural gas cooled to a liquid state for storage and transport. In railway applications, LNG can be used in dual-fuel engines that operate with both diesel and LNG, a configuration used in the converted Driving Power Cars of this train. The system is designed to replace about 40% of diesel consumption. The fuel arrangement is linked with lower emissions of carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulate matter in comparison with conventional diesel-only operation. Train Configuration and Trial Details The inaugural service was operated as an 8-coach, non-AC chair car train between Sabarmati and Mahesana Junction. Each converted Driving Power Car carries a 2,200-litre LNG tank with about 850-900 kg of usable LNG and a range of around 1,600 km on a full fill. More than 2,000 km of field trials were completed before the launch. These trials were conducted to test performance and reliability of the converted power cars under operational conditions. Railway Projects and Related Technologies The flagging-off was linked with railway development projects valued at over ₹1,472 crore or ₹1,542 crore. The package also included a WAG-12 locomotive maintenance shed and the Kavach train protection system. Kavach is an indigenous automatic train protection system used on Indian Railways to reduce the risk of signal passing at danger and collisions. WAG-12 is an electric freight locomotive class used by Indian Railways for heavy-haul operations. Important Facts for Exams Indian Railways launched its first hydrogen-powered train on 17 July 2026. LNG means liquefied natural gas, and it is stored at very low temperature in liquid form. The Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot converted the two 1,400 HP Driving Power Cars for dual-fuel operation. Indian Railways estimated annual savings of about ₹23.9 lakh for an eight-coach rake using the LNG dual-fuel system. Alternative Fuels in Indian Railways Indian Railways has been testing alternative propulsion systems such as LNG and hydrogen for rail transport. The LNG train adds to the list of fuel-diversification projects in the railway sector. articles.title: India's First Port-Based E-Methanol Facility Announced - GKToday
articles.content: Home India’s First Port-Based E-Methanol Facility Announced India’s First Port-Based E-Methanol Facility Announced September 28, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 India’s first port-based e- methanol production facility is being developed at Deendayal Port Authority in Kandla, Gujarat. The project is a joint initiative of Deendayal Port Authority, with 76% ownership, and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd, with 24% ownership. The total investment for the project is ₹2,300 crore, and the planned production capacity is 150 tonnes per day. E- Methanol as a Fuel E-methanol is a synthetic form of methanol produced using renewable power, water, and biogenic carbon dioxide. Methanol is an alcohol with the chemical formula CH3OH and is used as an industrial feedstock and marine fuel. Green methanol is one of the alternative fuels being considered for shipping and heavy transport. Project Phases and Capacity The project will be executed in two phases. Phase I involves a 50 tonnes per day unit with an estimated cost of ₹1,200 crore and a target completion date of January 2027. Phase II will add 100 tonnes per day at a cost of ₹1,100 crore and is targeted for completion by March 2027. The combined output will reach 150 tonnes per day after both phases are completed. Port-Based Green Fuel Infrastructure Deendayal Port Authority is located at Kandla in Gujarat and functions under India’s major port system. Port-based fuel facilities are linked to maritime bunkering, storage, and supply operations for vessels. The e-methanol from this project is planned for supply to ships operating on the Asia-Europe International Trade Corridor. Important Facts for Exams Deendayal Port Authority is one of India’s major ports and is located at Kandla in Gujarat. Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd is a public sector company associated with petrochemical production in India. Methanol is a single-carbon alcohol and is used in chemicals, fuels, and industrial processes. India has set a net-zero emissions target for 2070. Related Maritime Green Fuel Facility V.O. Chidambaranar Port in Tuticorin has also taken up a pilot Green Methanol Bunkering and Refuelling Facility. The project is linked to cleaner fuel use in the maritime sector and to bunkering operations at Indian ports. Shah said an 11,000-kilometre rail corridor was being converted into a four-track network to improve traffic movement and operational efficiency. The statement did not specify the sections included in this conversion or provide a completion timeline for the entire programme. He said diesel consumption was expected to reach zero by 2030, which would reduce foreign-exchange expenditure. The figures and target were presented at the event and were not accompanied in the report by a separate project-wise implementation plan. Railway electrification has reached 99.6%, according to Shah, with the remaining network expected to be electrified soon. He compared India’s reported electrification level with figures cited for China, Spain, France and the United Kingdom, saying India was on course to achieve full electrification. articles.title: Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG-powered train from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Station
articles.content: A hmedabad (Gujarat) [India], September 27 (ANI): Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off the country's first LNG (Liquefied Natural Gas)-powered train from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Railway Station on Sunday, alongside launching several other Indian Railways projects in the Sabarmati Division. Advertisement Speaking on the occasion, Shah said the projects addressed environmental concerns, passenger convenience and safety. "Today marks the launch of various Indian Railways projects within the Sabarmati Division. These initiatives address environmental concerns, enhance passenger convenience, and bolster safety. In the past, I have frequently disembarked at Sabarmati Railway Station while travelling from Delhi. I extend my heartiest congratulations to the entire team, from the Sabarmati Railway Division to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, because seeing Sabarmati Station now, after so long, is remarkable," he said. Shah added that the station and its facilities had undergone a complete transformation with an investment of ₹1,472 crore. "A radical transformation has been achieved regarding passenger convenience, safety, and connectivity. The projects inaugurated and those for which foundation stones were laid today, involving an investment of ₹1,472 crore, will prove immensely beneficial for passengers in this region," he said. Highlighting the Railways' progress on reducing diesel dependency and expanding electrification, Shah said the railways' consumption of diesel has dropped from 293 crore litres to 108 crore. He stated, "In 2015-16, the railways consumed 293 crore litres of diesel. That figure has now dropped to 108 crore in 2024-25, and by 2030, we will bring it down to zero, thereby saving Indian currency. This is a massive achievement that often goes unnoticed." He further said, "Electrification covered just 75 kilometres in 2010-11, whereas in 2023-24, we electrified 7,188 kilometres in a single year. 99.6 per cent of the railway network is already electrified. We will complete the remaining 0.3 per cent as well. Only Sweden has achieved 100 per cent electrification globally, but there is a tenfold difference between the scale of Sweden's rail network and ours." Shah also took a swipe at the Congress over its track record on development. "The people of this country should question the Congress members, who spout all sorts of nonsense, about this vast disparity in development. In their last ten years, they did nothing but engage in scams, scandals, and corruption amounting to ₹12 lakh crore; yet, in 12 years, no one has been able to level even the slightest allegation of corruption against PM Modi," he said. Earlier in the day, Shah also attended a programme organised on the occasion of Acharya Shri Padmasagar Surishwar Ji Maharaj's 92nd birthday in Ahmedabad. (ANI)
